div.head: Iudex 9
div.ab: Forneah ða earman men beoð wyrs bereafode fram þam unrihtwisan deman þonne fram þam wælgrimmestan here: ne bið nan heretoga swa gifre on fræmdrea manna yrfe swa se unrihtwisa dema byþ on his hyremanna.
Grauius enim lacerantur pauperes a prauis iudicibus quam a cruentis hostibus; nullus hostis acerbior, nulla pestis efficatior quam familiaris inimicus.

Die armen Leute werden von dem ungerechten Richter fast noch schlimmer beraubt als von dem grausamsten [Feindes- bes. Dänen-]heer: kein [feindlicher] Heerführer ist nach fremder Leute Habe so gierig, wie [es] der ungerechte Richter ist nach [der] seiner [Bezirks-] Eingesessenen.

The poor are robbed by the unjust judge almost worse than by the cruellest [enemy, especially Danish] army: no [enemy] army-leader is so greedy for strangers' property as the unjust judge is for [that] of his own [district's] inhabitants.
The poor are robbed almost worse by the unjust judge than by the cruellest army. No military leader is as greedy for the property of others as the unjust judge is for [the property of] his subjects.

Quadr. takes for as a particle, as in Middle English, like MS A at II Cn. 84, 1a

Um so verworfener der nach dem Gute eigener Landsleute gierige Richter! Da der Agsa. mit dem Worte ‘Heerführer’ von Isidor abweicht, so meint er wohl eine wirkliche Erfahrung, also die Dänengefahr. Noch deutlicher ist diese 9, 1 unter here, dem technischen Namen der Nordischen Eindringlinge, verstanden.—Auspressung der Untertanen geisselt weiterhin u. 9, 1—13. Gerefan rypað þa carman butan ælcere scylde, während sie vor 975 ne dorston strynan on unriht; Polity 12

All the more depraved, then, is the judge who covets the property of his own countrymen! Since the Anglo-Saxon departs from Isidor with the word ‘army-leader’, he probably means an actual experience, i.e. the Danish danger. This is understood still more clearly in 9, 1 under here, the technical name for the Northern invaders.—The extortion of subjects is castigated further below 9, 1—13.
